audits.title: 3484 Optimising neck of femur fractures surgical timing for improved patient outcomes: an excellence of service clinical audit
audits.setting: Southampton General Hospital, Major Trauma Centre

cycle1.result: Mean time to surgery 80 hours; surgical delays in 57.4%; 30-day mortality 4.7%.

audits.intervention: Additional theatre allocation, dedicated hip fracture team, multidisciplinary medical evaluation, optimised imaging, management of pre-existing conditions and standardised anticoagulation reversal.

cycle2.result: Mean time to surgery 55 hours; delayed surgeries 63.9%; 30-day mortality 3.0% (national average 5.9%).

audits.other_findings: Delays correlated with longer length of stay in both cycles; six deaths in each of the non-delayed (5.7%) and delayed (3.2%) groups post-intervention.
audits.citation: Jamal M, Tariq M, Kandel S, Ali M, Patel H. 3484 Optimising neck of femur fractures surgical timing for improved patient outcomes: an excellence of service clinical audit. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.081.

audits.title: "Early Trigger" Intravenous Vitamin K: Optimizing Target-Driven Care in Warfarinised Patients With Hip Fracture.
audits.standard: Hip fracture best practice tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission
audits.setting: Hip fracture unit, James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough

cycle1.result: Warfarinised patients on oral vitamin K protocol: mean time to theatre 53.71 hours; 79% breached BPT due to anticoagulation.

audits.intervention: Nurse-led 'early trigger' protocol giving 2 mg intravenous vitamin K in the emergency department before the INR result, added to the fast-track pathway.

cycle2.result: Mean time to theatre 37.61 hours (p<0.0001); 34% breached BPT due to anticoagulation; 21 (50%) operated within 36 hours and 33 (79%) within 48 hours.

audits.other_findings: No thromboembolic complications or deaths attributed to the protocol; 10 patients were delayed purely by inadequate reversal. Non-warfarinised controls (n=403) had mean time to theatre 28.36 hours.
audits.citation: Diament M, MacLeod K, O'Hare J, Tate A, Eardley W. "Early Trigger" Intravenous Vitamin K: Optimizing Target-Driven Care in Warfarinised Patients With Hip Fracture. Geriatr Orthop Surg Rehabil. 2015;6(4):263-268. doi:10.1177/2151458515595669. PMID: 26623160.

audits.title: Crossing quartiles: Improving time to theatre for patients with hip fractures in a large UK district general hospital; A quality improvement report.
audits.standard: Hip fracture Best Practice Tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission (National Hip Fracture Database)
audits.setting: Pinderfields General Hospital, Mid Yorkshire Hospitals NHS Trust (large district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Surgery within 36 hours 54%; mean time to surgery 43.68 hours; BPT achieved in 45.7%; trust ranked 152/160 for time to surgery.

audits.intervention: Anaesthetic 'hot week' introduced in January 2018: the same anaesthetist covers hip fracture lists, attends trauma meeting, liaises with orthopaedic and orthogeriatric teams and advises on medical optimisation.

cycle2.result: Surgery within 36 hours 87.5%; mean time to surgery 25.11 hours; BPT achieved in 84%; ranking rose to 20th for time to surgery and 18th for BPT.

audits.other_findings: Rescheduled operations fell from 126 to 31 and mean length of stay fell by 5.1 days; mortality unchanged. The unit sees on average 551 hip fractures a year. Abstract only.
audits.citation: Anthony C, Malaj M, Lokanathan P, Murgatroyd J, O'Connor P. Crossing quartiles: Improving time to theatre for patients with hip fractures in a large UK district general hospital; A quality improvement report. Injury. 2021;52(11):3415-3419. doi:10.1016/j.injury.2021.08.015. PMID: 34417002.

audits.title: Quality improvement initiative: how the setting up of an anaesthesia consultant-led perioperative outreach service addressed anaesthesia-specific issues to improve anaesthesia consult and surgery timings for hip fracture patients.
audits.standard: Surgery within 48 hours of hip fracture; aims of a 10% increase in patients seen by anaesthesia within 24 hours and a 10% increase in surgery within 48 hours
audits.setting: Changi General Hospital, 1000-bed hospital in eastern Singapore; anaesthesia department QI project

cycle1.result: Median time to first anaesthesia consult 35.3 hours; consults <24 hours 39%; median time to surgery 61.5 hours; surgery within 48 hours 38%.

audits.intervention: Consultant-led anaesthesia perioperative outreach service seeing patients within 24 hours of admission, with case manager notification, REDCap follow-up database, standardised workflow and guidelines, and 6-monthly PDSA audits.

cycle2.result: Median time to anaesthesia consult 21.5 hours (p = 0.029); consults <24 hours 67% (p < 0.003); median time to surgery 46 hours in results (50 hours in abstract) (p = 0.897); surgery within 48 hours 51.6% (p = 0.904).

audits.other_findings: Median time to nerve block fell from 41 hours (2019) to 22 hours (2021); patients discharged within 10 days rose from 53.5% to 59.5%. Critical care reviews rose while ICU admissions fell.
audits.citation: Siow WS, Tay L, Mah CL. Quality improvement initiative: how the setting up of an anaesthesia consultant-led perioperative outreach service addressed anaesthesia-specific issues to improve anaesthesia consult and surgery timings for hip fracture patients. BMJ Open Qual. 2022;11(3):e001738. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001738. PMID: 35940697.

audits.title: The impact of direct oral anticoagulants on hip fracture care in Australia and New Zealand: a prospective patient sprint audit.
audits.standard: ANZ hip fracture clinical care standard and international consensus: surgery within 36 hours (including for patients on DOACs)
audits.setting: Sprint audit of 31 hospitals (24 Australia, 7 New Zealand) in the Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry; patients on DOACs versus other or no antithrombotics

cycle1.result: Median time to surgery 39 h (IQR 24–48) on DOACs, 25 h (IQR 20–39) on no antithrombotic and 27 h (IQR 20–44) on other antithrombotics; DOAC patients had higher odds of surgery >36 h (aOR 3.65, 95% CI 2.40–5.55); 43% of DOAC patients had surgery within 36 h versus 61% on other antithrombotics.

audits.other_findings: 18% (192) were on DOACs; transfusion rates did not differ (23% vs 17% vs 22%). Only 5/24 Australian and all 7 New Zealand hospitals had a DOAC protocol, and 73% restarted DOACs >48 h after surgery.
audits.citation: Wijekulasuriya S, Seymour H, Tarrant S, Balogh ZJ, Navarre P, Hallen J, et al.. The impact of direct oral anticoagulants on hip fracture care in Australia and New Zealand: a prospective patient sprint audit. Osteoporos Int. 2025;36(11):2137-2147. doi:10.1007/s00198-025-07659-y. PMID: 40828478.

audits.title: International Normalized Ratio (INR) Sample Rejection in Neck of Femur Fracture Patients: A Retrospective Closed-Loop Study From a Major UK Trauma Centre.
audits.standard: Correct filling of 3.2% sodium citrate tubes to maintain 9:1 blood-to-anticoagulant ratio, with discard tube first when using butterfly sets; no numerical target stated
audits.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics Department, Heartlands Hospital, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (major trauma centre)

cycle1.result: 66/399 INR samples rejected (16.5%, 95% CI 13.2-20.5%); 62 (94%) for underfilling and 4 (6%) for haemolysis.

audits.intervention: Education sessions for junior doctors, phlebotomists and nurses on discard-tube use with butterfly sets, routine stocking of short-tubing collection devices, and visual reminder prompts at sampling points.

cycle2.result: 29/261 rejected (11.1%, 95% CI 7.8-15.5%); absolute reduction 5.4 percentage points, relative ~33%, not significant (p ≈ 0.11); 27 (93%) underfilling, 2 (7%) haemolysis.

audits.other_findings: Among anticoagulated patients rejection rose from 17.4% to 19.6%; underfilling remained the dominant cause.
audits.citation: Mersal M, Salama S, Alsonbaty M, Embaby O, Embabi A, Labidi M. International Normalized Ratio (INR) Sample Rejection in Neck of Femur Fracture Patients: A Retrospective Closed-Loop Study From a Major UK Trauma Centre. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e97097. doi:10.7759/cureus.97097. PMID: 41416323.

audits.title: Use of Pre-operative Echocardiograms in Traumatic Neck of Femur Fracture Patients: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Local trust guideline: no surgical delay awaiting echo; TTE only for listed indications; all TTE reports acknowledged by the anaesthetist; target 100%
audits.setting: District general hospital, patients aged 60 or over with neck of femur fracture who had pre-operative TTE

cycle1.result: No surgical delay 12/12 (100%); appropriate requests 4/12 (33.3%); reports acknowledged by anaesthetist 10/12 (83.3%).

audits.intervention: Teaching sessions, posters of request criteria, dissemination of audit findings, reminders at safety meetings and printed prompt cards.

cycle2.result: No surgical delay 17/17 (100%); appropriate requests 16/17 (94.1%); reports acknowledged 12/17 (70.6%).

audits.other_findings: Acknowledgement of echo reports fell. TTE findings changed anaesthetic management in 4/17 (23.5%), mainly invasive arterial monitoring.
audits.citation: Saeed A, Naureen M, Ali S, Wilson Z, Saeed R. Use of Pre-operative Echocardiograms in Traumatic Neck of Femur Fracture Patients: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2026;18(1):e101171. doi:10.7759/cureus.101171. PMID: 41664757.
